exposure: elective cesarean with or without an operative vaginal attempt
emergency cesarean with or without an operative vaginal attempt
cohort: 1,080,503 births in Quebec, Canada, between 2006 and 2019
finding: Operative vaginal delivery was associated with an increased risk of severe birth injury compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Both forceps and vacuum deliveries were associated with an increased risk of severe birth injury, with forceps carrying a higher risk for intracranial hemorrhage and brain/spinal damage and vacuum carrying a higher risk for epicranial subaponeurotic hemorrhage and skull fractures; emergency cesarean after an unsuccessful operative vaginal attempt was associated with intracranial and epicranial subaponeurotic hemorrhage.
